name: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport
before:
The main airport of Northeast India, at Borjhar about 28 km from Guwahati and 26 km from Dispur. It is managed by the Airports Authority of India and doubles as an Indian Air Force base.

Terminal 2 is the reason to look at this airport again. Designed by Nuru Karim, it takes its shape from Assam's kopou phool, the foxtail orchid, and uses more than 140 tonnes of bamboo, drawing on Assam's bholuka bamboo craft and the building techniques of the Apatani people of Arunachal Pradesh. It won an International Architecture Award in 2025. Inside there are ten air bridges and sixteen self service bag drops.

Terminal 1 has been in service since 1958. It covers 28,685 square metres across three levels, with arrivals on the ground floor, the boarding area on the mezzanine and departures above, and four air bridges. It is rated for six million passengers a year.

The airport is named after Gopinath Bordoloi, the independence activist who became Assam's first Chief Minister after independence.
after:
The main airport of Northeast India, at Borjhar about 28 km from Guwahati. It is run by the Adani group on a 50-year lease from the Airports Authority of India, and doubles as an Indian Air Force base.

Terminal 2, inaugurated in December 2025, is built for 13.1 million passengers a year, and the airport now lists its airlines there. Designed by Nuru Karim, it draws on Assam's foxtail orchid (kopou phool) and uses more than 140 tonnes of bamboo, with elements of Assam's bholuka bamboo craft and the building methods of the Apatani people of Arunachal Pradesh. It won an International Architecture Award in 2025.

The airport dates from 1958 and is named after Gopinath Bordoloi, the independence activist who became Assam's first Chief Minister.

claims.claim: the main airport of Northeast India
claims.inAfter: The main airport of Northeast India
claims.note: AAI's full-year table for April 2025 to March 2026 gives Guwahati 6.62 million passengers, over four times the next north-eastern airport (Agartala, 1.54 million; then Imphal, 1.37 million, and Dibrugarh, 0.84 million). Bagdogra (3.66 million) is in West Bengal, outside the north east. The operator calls it the largest airport in Assam and a doorway to the seven sister states.

The operator's airline table puts every airline it shows (Alliance Air, Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo, Akasa Air, SpiceJet, Thai AirAsia and Druk Air) at T2, and its home page gives waiting times for T2 only; the table has a 'Load More Airlines' button, so the text does not say 'all'.
